feedback.overall:
1. Overall assessment  
Strong, credible CV for a senior digital communications leader: clear positioning, relevant progression, and solid evidence of scope across strategy, platforms, analytics, and multimedia. Writing is polished overall, but impact would improve with more outcome-focused metrics, less repetition across skills sections, and a few consistency edits.

1. Top strengths  
- Clear senior-level narrative with logical progression at NACo and a strong headline/profile aligned to target roles.  
- Good credibility through concrete scope indicators: 10,000+ page migration, 3.5M annual page views, 50+ publishers, analytics stack, and studio buildout.  
- Writing is generally concise and professional, with strong domain vocabulary in digital strategy, governance, advocacy, and CMS modernization.

1. Top improvements  
- Add more measurable outcomes beyond scope: e.g., traffic growth, email performance, engagement lifts, cost/time savings, adoption rates, or campaign results.  
- Reduce duplication between “Core Competencies,” “Topline Skills,” and “Technical + IT”; consolidate to tighten structure and save space.  
- Fix consistency/style issues: “12 years experience” should be “12 years’ experience” or “12+ years of experience”; maintain consistent comma usage in lists (“workflows and systems” vs. “workflows, and systems”); consider standardizing date format (“Oct. 2024 – Present” vs. “Sept.”/“Mar.”). No major misspellings or obvious typos found.
feedback.intro:
Quick assessment: Strong, credible summary that aligns well with the CV, but it is slightly generic and repeats language already covered in Core Competencies and Topline Skills. It would be stronger with one clearer differentiator tied to recent senior-level work.

Suggested rewrite improvements:
- Change “more than 12 years experience” to “12+ years of experience.”
- Lead with current senior value: digital strategy, platform modernization, and communications operations for mission-driven/public-sector organizations.
- Tighten the channel list to avoid sounding like a skills inventory; emphasize outcomes and scope instead.
- Suggested rewrite: “Digital communications and strategy leader with 12+ years of experience leading web, content, email, social media, and multimedia programs for mission-driven organizations. Brings deep expertise in cross-channel strategy, platform modernization, and the workflows, governance, and analytics that support complex communications operations. Strong background in advocacy messaging, stakeholder coordination, and translating technical or policy issues into clear, accessible content.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Cross-channel communications,” “platform modernization,” and workflow/systems language overlap heavily with Core Competencies and Topline Skills.
- The long channel list repeats detail already demonstrated throughout Work Experience.
feedback.coreCompetencies:
Quick assessment: Strong, relevant themes, but this block is broad and overlaps heavily with the summary, Topline Skills, and Soft Skills. Tightening wording and emphasizing leadership-level capabilities will make it more distinctive and impactful.

Suggested rewrite improvements:
- Use parallel, noun-based phrasing and pluralize where appropriate: “Multi-channel communications,” “Web platform & CMS administration,” “Analytics, reporting & optimization.”
- Replace vague items with sharper leadership terms: “Workflow & systems architecture” → “Content operations & workflow architecture”; “Stakeholder & cross-department coordination” → “Cross-functional stakeholder leadership.”
- Prioritize most marketable strengths first: Digital strategy & transformation • Enterprise web platforms • Editorial systems & governance • Analytics & optimization.
- Suggested rewrite: Digital strategy & transformation • Enterprise web platforms & CMS administration • Editorial systems & governance • Multi-channel communications • Analytics, reporting & optimization • Content operations & workflow architecture • Cross-functional stakeholder leadership • Policy & advocacy communications • Multimedia & live event production

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Stakeholder & cross-department coordination” overlaps with Soft Skills.
- Several items repeat Topline Skills almost verbatim; consider using this section as a shorter headline-style summary only.

items.title: Strategic Communications Consultant
items.subtitle: Freelance (full-time engagement)
items.content:
Support a U.S.-based national membership organization on digital strategy, campaign platforms, content operations and enterprise web improvement.
- Build and refine digital systems, workflows and analytics that support coordinated organization-wide communications.
- Develop campaign and storytelling experiences within the organization’s Drupal platform, including custom microsite structures, modular content sections and downloadable member-facing toolkits.
- Deliver CMS development, front-end implementation and technical troubleshooting for large public-facing web properties.
- Advise on governance, usability and operational best practices across web, email, social and multimedia channels.
- Lead development of an AI-enabled search initiative, shaping retrieval strategy, structured content workflows and user-facing discovery design.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong, current role with clear relevance to your headline, but it reads broad and overlaps heavily with the “Recent Projects” section and prior NACo work. Tighten it around scope, technical leadership, and outcomes; let projects carry the examples.

Suggested edit:
- Open with a sharper summary: “Lead digital strategy, Drupal platform development, and communications systems modernization for a U.S. national membership organization.”
- Collapse overlapping bullets into 4–5 impact-focused lines; e.g. combine systems/workflows/analytics/governance into one bullet about improving cross-channel operations.
- Rephrase for ownership and outcomes: “Built Drupal campaign microsites, modular content components, and member toolkits to support scalable storytelling and advocacy campaigns.”
- Add measurable signals where possible: site size, stakeholder groups served, workflow efficiency gains, search/discovery improvements, or number of channels/platforms supported.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “AI-enabled search initiative” duplicates the Recent Projects rail; keep one brief mention here and leave detail there.
- Drupal microsites, storytelling modules, and toolkits also overlap with “We Are Counties Microsite”; avoid repeating feature lists in both places.

items.title: Director of Digital Media
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content:
Led NACo’s digital communications team, overseeing the organization’s website, email, social media and video platforms, along with digital strategy, analytics, governance and budget management.
- Led the redesign and migration of NACo’s 10,000+ page website into a new Drupal platform supporting 3.5 million annual page views, 6,000+ average daily users and 50+ internal publishers.
- Directed NACo’s core digital communications channels, including email newsletters reaching tens of thousands of county officials and social media platforms serving thousands of followers.
- Built NACo’s first broadcast-quality in-house video studio, expanding in-house capacity for advocacy programming, event production and recurring multimedia content.
- Expanded the organization’s analytics infrastructure across GA4, Microsoft Clarity, Power BI, Looker Studio and BigQuery, improving reporting and strategic decision-making.
- Strengthened digital operations through clearer governance, publishing standards and cross-department planning systems.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong, high-impact leadership entry with good scale signals. It should be tightened around 3–4 biggest outcomes and framed to show progression beyond your earlier NACo roles.

Suggested edit:
- Open with a sharper summary: “Directed NACo’s digital communications function across web, email, social, video, analytics, governance, and budget management.”
- Consolidate channel oversight into one impact bullet and prioritize measurable outcomes: website migration, audience scale, publisher count, reporting stack, studio launch.
- Rewrite bullets with action + result structure, e.g.:
- “Led redesign and migration of NACo’s 10,000+ page website to Drupal, supporting 3.5M annual page views, 6,000+ daily users, and 50+ internal publishers.”
- “Built NACo’s first broadcast-quality in-house studio, increasing capacity for advocacy programming, event production, and recurring multimedia content.”
- “Implemented analytics stack across GA4, Clarity, Power BI, Looker Studio, and BigQuery to improve performance reporting and decision-making.”
- If available, add metrics for email growth, social engagement, production volume, budget size, or efficiency gains.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Directed core digital communications channels” overlaps with the prior NACo role; keep this version focused on enterprise leadership and transformation.
- Governance/editorial workflow language also appears elsewhere; emphasize standards at scale or cross-department operating model.

items.title: Associate Communications Director
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content:
Led day-to-day digital communications operations across web, email, social media and video, helping scale NACo’s editorial coordination and advocacy communications.
- Managed four recurring weekly newsletters reaching tens of thousands of county officials and public-sector stakeholders.
- Produced and expanded a weekly advocacy video update, helping establish video as a recurring policy communications channel.
- Strengthened editorial planning and coordination across communications, advocacy and program teams.
- Helped improve the consistency and effectiveness of NACo’s digital publishing workflows.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong progression story, but this entry overlaps heavily with the later Director role and earlier digital/media role. Make it more distinct by emphasizing executional leadership, channel ownership, and systems/process improvements that set up the later promotion.

Suggested edit
- Rewrite the lead to focus on scope and progression: “Managed NACo’s day-to-day digital communications across web, email, social and video, leading editorial execution and cross-team coordination for advocacy and member communications.”
- Tighten bullets around concrete ownership: “Managed four weekly newsletters reaching tens of thousands of county officials and public-sector stakeholders.”
- Make the video bullet outcome-focused: “Launched and grew a weekly advocacy video update, establishing video as a recurring policy communications channel.”
- Replace weaker phrasing like “helped improve” with direct action if accurate: “Built more consistent digital publishing workflows and editorial planning processes across communications, advocacy and program teams.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings
- Avoid repeating broad channel oversight already covered in the Director of Digital Media role.
- “Weekly video updates” also appears in the 2015–2018 role; distinguish this entry as scaling/formalizing the program, not starting it.

items.title: Digital Strategy & Content Leadership
items.content:
- Enterprise digital strategy
- Editorial systems and governance
- Multi-channel communications leadership
- Public-sector and advocacy messaging
- Audience-focused content planning
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong themes, but this item overlaps heavily with the header and Core Competencies. It should be tightened to emphasize senior leadership scope and audience/governance strengths without repeating platform or analytics language covered elsewhere.

Suggested edit:
- Replace with sharper, less generic phrasing:
- Enterprise digital strategy
- Editorial governance and content operations
- Cross-channel communications leadership
- Public-sector and advocacy communications
- Audience-centered content strategy
- Consider swapping “messaging” for “communications” to sound more senior and operationally aligned with recent roles.
- Use “content operations” instead of “content planning” to better reflect leadership in workflows, governance, and execution.
- Keep this section purely strategic; save tools, platforms, and analytics terms for the other skills blocks.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Enterprise digital strategy” and “editorial systems and governance” already echo the header/Core Competencies; rephrasing to “content operations” and “editorial governance” helps reduce repetition.
- “Multi-channel communications leadership” overlaps with Core Competencies’ “Multi-channel communications operations.”

items.title: Web Platforms & Technical Execution
items.content:

- WordPress
- SharePoint

- Workflow automation
- Airtable systems
- AI-enabled search experiences
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong category, but it reads like a raw tool dump and overlaps heavily with the Technical + IT section. For a topline skills item, emphasize higher-value platform leadership and current strengths rather than listing every technology.

Suggested edit:
- Rewrite as a tighter, impact-oriented line: Drupal • CMS modernization & migration • Front-end implementation (HTML, CSS, JavaScript) • API integrations & workflow automation • Airtable systems • AI-enabled search experiences
- Remove lower-priority or older/platform-specific items here if they are not central to recent work, especially WordPress, SharePoint, Power Pages, and jQuery.
- Replace “Technical Execution” with “Platform Modernization & Technical Delivery” to better match recent Drupal, AI search, and systems work.
- If space allows, group by capability over tools: CMS platforms, front-end implementation, integrations/automation, AI search.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This item duplicates the Technical + IT section almost verbatim; keep Topline Skills broader and reserve full tool lists for Technical + IT.
- “CMS modernization,” “workflow automation,” and “AI-enabled search experiences” also echo Core Competencies; avoid repeating the same phrasing exactly.

items.title: Analytics, Insights & Optimization
items.content:
- GA4
- Microsoft Clarity
- Looker Studio
- Power BI
- BigQuery
- KPI design
- Leadership reporting
- SEO and performance analysis
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong, relevant tools list, but it reads as a generic keyword block and overlaps heavily with the “Technical + IT” analytics section. In Topline Skills, this should emphasize higher-value capability and decision impact, not just platforms.

Suggested edit
- Reframe from tool list to capability-led phrasing: “Analytics strategy, KPI design, executive reporting, SEO/performance analysis.”
- Keep only the most credible core tools after the capability terms: “GA4, BigQuery, Looker Studio, Power BI, Microsoft Clarity.”
- Tighten wording and group related items: “Executive dashboards & leadership reporting” is stronger than “Leadership reporting.”
- Optional rewrite: “Analytics strategy & KPI design • Executive dashboards and leadership reporting • GA4, BigQuery, Looker Studio, Power BI, Microsoft Clarity • SEO and digital performance analysis”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings
- This largely duplicates “Technical + IT > Data, Analytics & Optimization”; use Topline Skills for strategic positioning and leave fuller tool inventory to Technical + IT.
- “Analytics and reporting infrastructure” already appears in Core Competencies, so avoid repeating that exact framing.

items.title: University of Virginia
items.subtitle: Bachelor of Arts (BA), Economics & History
items.content: Ranked among the top public universities in the United States
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: The current line adds little value and reads like generic school marketing. For an experienced candidate, this education entry should be minimal and factual unless you have honors or distinctions worth adding.

Suggested edit:
- Replace the content line entirely with no body text; the degree, school, location, and dates are sufficient.
- If applicable, swap in a concrete credential instead: “Relevant coursework: …” or “Honors: …” only if genuinely strong and still relevant.
- Tighten the subtitle to “B.A., Economics and History” for cleaner formatting.
- Consider dropping dates if you want to reduce age signaling and keep focus on recent senior experience.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Ranked among the top public universities…” is generic and not candidate-specific, so it weakens the entry rather than strengthening it.
- Avoid adding coursework unless it clearly supports current digital strategy/communications work; otherwise it will feel disconnected from the stronger recent experience.

items.title: Web Platforms & CMS
items.content: Drupal • WordPress • SharePoint • Power Pages • GitHub Pages
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid platform list, but it’s too generic and currently duplicates the “Web Platforms & Technical Execution” topline skills section. Use this item to signal depth and recency, especially Drupal, rather than repeating a flat list.

Suggested edit
- Reorder by strongest/recent relevance: Drupal • WordPress • SharePoint • Power Pages • GitHub Pages
- Add light qualifiers to show level without overloading: “Drupal (enterprise migrations, microsites, governance)” • “WordPress” • “SharePoint” • “Power Pages” • “GitHub Pages”
- If space allows, make it outcome-oriented: “Drupal (10,000+ page migration; campaign microsites)” to connect directly to recent impact.
- Consider renaming the heading to “CMS Platforms” for tighter phrasing.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings
- This largely repeats “Web Platforms & Technical Execution” in Topline Skills; differentiate this section with proficiency/context, not the same nouns.
- Avoid adding “CMS modernization” or “AI-enabled search” here since those already appear elsewhere and are better supported in experience bullets.

items.title: Coding & Technical Implementation
items.content: HTML5 • CSS3 • JavaScript • jQuery • API integrations • Google Tag Manager • Cloudflare Workers • GitHub Actions
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid technical range, but this item reads like a generic keyword list and overlaps heavily with “Web Platforms & Technical Execution.” Make it more current and implementation-focused by emphasizing tools that support recent work and trimming older/basic terms.

Suggested edit:
- Rewrite as: “Front-end implementation: JavaScript, HTML/CSS, API integrations, Google Tag Manager, Cloudflare Workers, GitHub Actions”
- Drop versioned/basic labels (“HTML5,” “CSS3”) unless required by the role; they add little senior-level value.
- Consider replacing “jQuery” with “legacy jQuery” or removing it if not central to current work; it can date the profile.
- If accurate, add one higher-value qualifier tied to impact, e.g., “deployment automation,” “serverless scripting,” or “tagging/measurement implementation.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This duplicates “HTML, CSS, JavaScript and jQuery” and “API integrations” already listed under Topline Skills.
- “Google Tag Manager” may fit better under “Data, Analytics & Optimization” unless you want this section strictly implementation-oriented.

items.title: Automation & Workflow Systems
items.content: Airtable • Power Automate • Zapier • Jira • Asana • Basecamp • Slack • Teams • Trello
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid tool coverage, but this reads as a generic software list rather than evidence of workflow systems capability. It also overlaps with “Workflow automation and platform integration” in Core Competencies and “Airtable systems / Workflow automation” in Topline Skills.

Suggested edit:
- Rename to: Automation, Workflow & Collaboration Tools
- Group by function to improve scanability: Airtable, Power Automate, Zapier • Jira, Asana, Trello, Basecamp • Slack, Microsoft Teams
- If space allows, add a light qualifier tied to recent work: Used to build cross-team workflows, automate handoffs, and support editorial/project coordination
- Keep only the strongest, most relevant tools; consider dropping older/general collaboration apps if not central to current work

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Airtable” and “workflow automation” already appear in Topline Skills; avoid repeating the same phrasing here
- Slack/Teams are common workplace tools; if space is tight, prioritize actual automation/project systems over chat platforms

items.title: Email & Engagement Systems
items.content: Dynamics 365 Customer Insights / Journeys • Higher Logic • Mailchimp
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: The item is clear but too bare to add much value on its own. Since email leadership already appears in recent NACo roles, this line should stay concise and tool-focused rather than restating channel ownership.

Suggested edit
- Rename to: Email Marketing & Engagement Platforms
- Tighten platform naming for readability and ATS consistency: Microsoft Dynamics 365 Customer Insights & Journeys • Higher Logic • Mailchimp
- If accurate, consider separating enterprise vs. SMB tools by emphasis order: Higher Logic • Microsoft Dynamics 365 Customer Insights & Journeys • Mailchimp
- Only add a qualifier if it reflects real depth, e.g., campaign automation, newsletter operations, or audience segmentation

Duplicate/redundancy warnings
- Avoid adding “email newsletters,” “audience engagement,” or campaign management language here; that is already covered in Work Experience.
- If Dynamics 365 was limited exposure, don’t over-position it alongside stronger hands-on platforms.

items.title: Work Eligibility
items.content: Full legal authorization to work in Belgium (Visa D + residence permit / carte de séjour)
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Useful for Belgium-based applications, but the phrasing is a bit legalistic and takes more space than needed. This should read as a clear status note, not a headline achievement.

Suggested edit:
- Rewrite for brevity and recruiter scanability: “Authorized to work in Belgium (Visa D and residence permit).”
- If accurate, make it stronger and simpler: “Fully authorized to work in Belgium; residence permit in place.”
- Avoid the French term unless the role specifically requires bilingual administrative terminology; “residence permit” is usually enough.
- Consider moving this into the contact/header area for local applications, since eligibility matters more there than in a secondary rail.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- No major duplication, but this item is lower-value than recent experience; keep it very short so it doesn’t compete for attention.
- If location/contact already signals Belgium and applications are local, this may be optional rather than essential.

items.title: Languages
items.content:
**English** (Native)
**French** (A2/Learning)
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: This item is clear but too compressed and visually awkward. It should be reformatted for quick scanning and framed honestly so French supports your Belgium-based role without overstating proficiency.

Suggested edit
- Rewrite as a simple line: Languages: English (native) | French (A2, currently improving)
- Use lowercase proficiency style for consistency and cleaner tone: native, A2, conversational/basic if accurate.
- If relevant to target roles, add practical context only if true: French (A2, professional working improvement underway)
- Keep it concise; this section is supporting information, not a selling point versus your recent digital leadership experience.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings
- No major duplication, but avoid overdesign/bolding here; the CV already has strong skills sections competing for attention.
- If space is tight, this can stay in the rail and should not be repeated in the header, summary, or cover letter unless language is job-relevant.

items.title: Soft Skills
items.content: Cross-department coordination • Stakeholder communication • Team leadership • Strategic planning • Clear writing and editing • Problem-solving • Adaptability
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: This section is too generic and largely repeats strengths already proven in the summary and core competencies. On a senior CV, “soft skills” should either be removed or reframed as leadership traits tied to scope and outcomes.

Suggested edit:
- Rename to “Leadership Strengths” or “Management & Collaboration” to sound more senior and less filler.
- Cut generic items like “Problem-solving” and “Adaptability”; keep only traits that support target roles.
- Tighten to 4–5 items max, e.g.: Cross-functional leadership • Executive stakeholder management • Editorial judgment • Team development • Strategic planning
- If space is tight, remove this section entirely and use the room for quantified achievements in recent roles.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Cross-department coordination” and “Stakeholder communication” duplicate the header summary and Core Competencies.
- “Team leadership” and “Strategic planning” are already demonstrated more credibly in the 2022–2024 Director role.

items.title: References
items.content: References available upon request.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: This item adds little value and uses space that could better support recent, higher-impact experience. “References available upon request” is assumed by most employers and usually should be removed.

Suggested edit:
- Delete the “References” entry entirely.
- Use the freed space for stronger supporting content instead, such as a brief “Selected Results” rail item with 1–2 metrics from recent roles.
- If references are specifically requested, provide them separately rather than on the CV.
- If you want a replacement rail item, consider “Work Authorization” or “Languages,” which are more useful and already present here.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This section is redundant because reference availability is standard and does not differentiate you.
- Keeping it may weaken the second-page rail by displacing more relevant, recent qualifications.

items.title: Digital Media Manager / Producer
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content: Advanced through two digital roles, supporting the creation of the organization’s first in-house digital team and strengthening workflows across web, email, social, and multimedia. Contributed to a major website refresh and produced high-impact digital content—including livestreams and weekly video updates—while providing day-to-day guidance to a digital media associate.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong progression signal, but the item is still broad and overlaps with the 2018–2024 NACo roles. Make it more clearly early-career by emphasizing team-building support, production execution, and any concrete outputs.

Suggested edit:
- Rewrite to foreground scope and progression: “Promoted across two digital roles to help launch NACo’s first in-house digital team, supporting web, email, social and multimedia operations.”
- Add 1–2 measurable outcomes if available: website refresh scale, livestream/event volume, cadence of weekly videos, audience growth, or process improvements.
- Tighten phrasing and reduce generic claims like “high-impact” and “strengthening workflows”; replace with specifics such as “standardized publishing workflows” or “produced weekly advocacy videos and livestreamed major events.”
- Consider: “Supported a major website refresh, produced recurring video and livestream content, and provided day-to-day oversight for a digital media associate.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Weekly video updates” overlaps with the 2018–2022 role; distinguish this as launching/producing the series rather than expanding it.
- Avoid repeating broad multi-channel leadership already covered more strongly in later NACo roles.

items.title: County Solutions & Innovations Coordinator
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content: Coordinated innovation and research projects supporting organizational programs and policy work. Contributed to digital content production and multimedia materials, and launched the organization’s first podcast, overseeing planning, scripting, and production.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid early-career entry that shows initiative, especially the first podcast launch, but it reads generic and overlaps with later NACo digital/media roles. Emphasize the innovation/program support angle and keep the multimedia point focused on the standout first.

Suggested edit:
- Rewrite to foreground the distinctive achievement: “Coordinated county innovation and research initiatives supporting NACo program and policy teams.”
- Add a second sentence with clearer scope and action: “Produced digital and multimedia content to translate research into member-facing communications, including launching NACo’s first podcast and leading planning, scripting, and production.”
- If possible, add outcomes: number of projects supported, podcast episodes launched, audiences reached, or teams/stakeholders served.
- Tighten phrasing by removing “organizational programs and policy work” and “contributed to,” which are vague.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- Avoid broad “digital content production and multimedia materials” language that repeats later digital media roles.
- Don’t overstate video/media leadership here; later roles already show stronger, more recent ownership.
